title: Ask before deleting each file
summary: Use the interactive option of the rm command so the terminal asks y or n before it deletes each file. This protects files you want to keep.

aliases.text: confirm before rm deletes a file
terminal ask yes no before delete
как не удалить файл случайно в терминале

prerequisites: A terminal window is open (Terminal on macOS, any terminal app on Linux)

steps.explain: Find out which rm program this system runs. This is a read-only check; it only prints a path.
steps.expect: A path such as /bin/rm, /usr/bin/rm or /usr/sbin/rm. Any path means rm is installed.

steps.explain: Check that rm has the -i option. This is read-only. Look for a line that starts with -i and says it asks before each removal.
steps.expect: Linux: a line starting with -i (on some systems the words 'prompt before every removal' are on the next line). macOS: a line starting with -i about requesting confirmation before removing each file.

steps.explain: List the files in the current folder, so you can pick the one you want to delete. This only reads the list.
steps.expect: One line per file or folder. The file names are in the last column.

steps.explain: Delete one file, but only after you confirm. rm asks a question about this file. Type y and press Return to delete it. Type n and press Return, or just press Return, to keep it.

placeholders.name: FILE
placeholders.description: Name of one file to delete. Use one file at a time.

steps.expect: The terminal shows a question such as: rm: remove regular file 'notes.txt'? Nothing is deleted until you type y.

warnings: rm deletes files for good. Deleted files do not go to the Trash, so answer y only for files you really want to delete.
This card covers single files. The folder options of rm are not part of this card.
On macOS, -i asks only when you type in a terminal window.

source.title: rm manual; card written and verified in the lnxhelp sandbox
